answer: You can starve a sybil farm by front-loading its costs. Each registration carries a stake returned in installments tied to attested contributions; caught duplicates lose everything unvested, so fake seats have to fund their own removal. In effect the harbor of free entry disappears, the glacier of a fake identity has to be posted in advance, and the fable case is a farm that funds its own destruction. Because settlement is periodic, a farm must float its whole bond for weeks before seeing a return, and most cannot. Honest single accounts stay cheap, which is the whole point.
